processing: Typical of Darjeeling: orthodox black tea, withered, rolled, oxidised and dried, grown organically under the Chamong Group.
harvest_season: As across Darjeeling, first flush in spring and second flush from around May to June, followed by monsoon and autumn pickings.
appearance_dry: Twisted Darjeeling leaf in mixed olive and brown, as usual for the region.
appearance_liquor: Gold to amber, depending on the flush.
taste_profile: Few tasting records name this garden. Expect the general Darjeeling pattern: floral and brisk in spring, fruitier and fuller in summer.

brewing.notes: Brewed Western-style, as for other Darjeeling. Use cooler water and a shorter steep for first flush.

vintage_note: Little is recorded about how this garden's lots reach the shelf. As usual for Darjeeling, expect it to be sold by year and flush, and buy the latest harvest available.
description:
Bannockburn is an organic garden in the Lebong Valley of Darjeeling, and one of the older names there. It covers about 300 hectares, with around 143 under tea.

It belongs to the Chamong Group, a large organic producer in Darjeeling and Assam. No detailed account of the garden's own methods is easy to find, so assume the usual orthodox Darjeeling making.

The cup should follow the regional seasons: floral and light in spring, fuller and fruitier in summer. Those are notes for Darjeeling in general rather than a verdict on this garden, since few people have written about it specifically.

When you do see the name on a bag, check the year and the flush. A good seller should be able to tell you both.
history:
Bannockburn dates from the mid-nineteenth century, in the first phase of tea planting in Darjeeling. The name is said to recall the Scottish battlefield, a nod to where early European planters came from.

Annual output is put at about 90,000 kg. Today the garden is listed among the Darjeeling estates of the Chamong Group.
